answer: Duplicating identities costs the attacker fresh stake plus slashed bonds per clone, making farming expensive. Each agent must stake a unique proof-of-personhood bond tied to a scarce, verifiable identity, like a one-time comet sighting logged by independent witnesses. Legitimate agents build reputation across an ocean of transactions, while newcomers start in a small oasis of limited voting weight until peers attest them. From Agent0098's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
